review_note: Source states erotic-mode ZiTan is unfavorable to Tianxiang because feeling/sexual entanglement can affect career; relational drag and career consequence should be separated.
Source distinguishes integrated Tianliang as having better interpersonal relations and better opportunities; relation state and downstream development should be separated.
Source states solitary Tianliang dislikes LianSha and that malefic/Lianji conditions damage interpersonal relations and can create severe downstream setbacks.
Source explicitly calls Tiantong one of Tianliang's favorable periods and says even solitary mode can gain generative opportunity; this is a temporal projection, not a primitive state increase.
Source supports greater isolation/kinship difficulty and hardship under fallen or Hua-Ji Sun, but the canonical 'reputation pressure' label is broader than the source.
Source states bad Wupo can cause financial disputes and, under Lian/Wu double-Ji patterns, relationship rupture; separate relational and downstream outcome layers.
Source describes family/kin incidents for the harsh mode under a Sun period; keep as downstream traditional family projection.
Source says Sun with Ji is broadly an adverse period for both LianSha modes and instructs readers to use the twelve palaces to determine the concrete manifestation.
Source explicitly says harsh LianSha under Xing-Ji clamp tends to self-provoke disputes; four malefics can project to severe traditional risk labels.
Source states striving LianSha in Tianliang periods can build interpersonal relations or later support after setbacks; the main normalized target should be relational/support state.
Source describes kin illness/separation and family pain for harsh LianSha in Tianliang periods; retain only as downstream traditional projection.
Source says open-minded Tiantong can withstand Wupo adversity and turn misfortune toward favorable development through effort; resilience remains derived after A1.
Source explicitly contrasts open-minded Tiantong benefiting from good ZiTan with short-willed Tiantong falling into comfort/pleasure and career cooling.
Source states a Jumen year can bring promotion/opportunity to open-minded mode, while short-willed mode must act through its own effort to obtain opportunity.
No matching Lianxiang-good-support/cooperation rule was found in system 38 source span; the content resembles a rule from a different Tiantong system and should not execute.
Source says adaptable Wupo likes a Sun period so long as Sun is not Hua-Ji, often gaining a chance to establish a career base.
Source says Tianji-Taiyin periods generally allow adaptable Wupo to develop gradually and obtain benefit.
Source calls ZiTan a clearly favorable period for adaptable Wupo; downstream development opportunity is the appropriate layer.
Source says Ziwei Hua-Ke is favorable to both Wupo modes and can yield fame/profit; 'norm/reputation compensation' is an interpretive over-normalization.
Source supports Tianliang year as a possible breakthrough/change opportunity for adaptable Wupo; keep it at temporal projection level.
Source treats good Lianxiang as a favorable period for adaptable Wupo; retain as downstream opportunity.
Source explicitly links steady Sun to greater ability to accumulate wealth and social position; this is a downstream output.
Source says Tianfu is favorable to steady Sun and brings support/promotion from elders or superiors; relational support and stable development should be separated.
Source says steady Sun likes Tianji-Taiyin periods and can gain wealth/profit; treat planning/wealth effects as outputs.
Source says ZiTan is a competitive period for steady Sun, with outcome depending on actual configuration; downstream development/competition outcome only.
Source supports good Jumen as a favorable period for steady Sun, including external recognition/support and progress; separate support relation from outcome.
Source says steady Sun under good Tianxiang can still progress while encountering competition; separate cooperative/support context from position/development projection.
Source states floating Sun in a bad Tianxiang period can choose unsuitable partners and even encounter traditional litigation labels; separate relationship misjudgment from L3 legal projection.
Source supports health pressure for steady Sun in a Tianliang major period, but does not support the added 'responsibility load' normalization.
Source says good LianSha periods are generally favorable to Sun, steady mode being better able to maintain the gain.
Source says Tiantong is a favorable period for steady Sun and can mark the beginning of career establishment.
Source says Tianji-Taiyin without harmful transformation supports slow, stable development for modest Tianfu.
Source says good ZiTan is an important favorable period for modest Tianfu and can unfold latent capacity.
Source supports setbacks/failure pressure for timid Tianfu under bad Tianxiang, but not the stronger normalization 'support network collapse'.
Source says LianSha with Lu is favorable to Tianfu, especially modest mode, which can exercise responsibility/command more effectively.
Source says LianSha Hua-Ji is dangerous for Tianfu, with timid mode more prone to traditional litigation/conflict outcomes.
Source explicitly says a good LianSha year can become an enterprising opportunity for timid Tianfu.
Source says good Wupo can provide timid Tianfu a life-change opportunity, while strong Pojun can bring worry, labor and a sense of insufficient capacity.
Source says modest Tianfu likes an exalted Sun period and tends to become more active/developing.
Source says rational Ji-Yue particularly likes Tanlang Hua-Quan in a ZiTan period and regards it as a career opportunity.
Source says good Jumen can create a career-building period and that emotional mode with Fu-Bi/Kui-Yue can gain popularity/support.
Source says good Wupo benefits rational Ji-Yue in a major period and offers opportunity in a year.
Source explicitly separates rational vs emotional Ji-Yue under exalted/fallen Sun: opportunity/suppression for rational mode and openness/distress for emotional mode.
Source says good Qisha is favorable to both ZiXiang modes, with affective mode often gaining especially favorable change.
Source says Qisha with bad stars/Kong-Jie can produce career and relationship setbacks, especially for non-affective ZiXiang; downstream multi-domain projection.
Source says when Pojun is not natal Hua-Lu, affective ZiXiang can develop stably while non-affective ZiXiang can become more trapped the more it seeks change.
Source says stable Tianliang likes Qisha periods and can gain favorable change opportunity.
Source says unstable Tianliang in a Lianzhen period can feel emotionally unsettled and, with stronger malefics, project to career failure or traditional litigation labels.
Source says Pojun without heavy punishment/malefics can bring a good-quality transformation to either Tianliang mode.
Source says Tiantong with Tuoluo/malefics yields traditional health risk for unstable Tianliang but emotional unease for stable Tianliang.
